# randomPlantedForest

`randomPlantedForest` implements Random Planted Forest ([Hiabu, Mammen &
Meyer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.14563)), a tree ensemble whose
predictions you can read off directly. The explanation is exact and is
not a post-hoc approximation.

The fitted model is a short sum of main effects and interactions.
Interactions of order three or higher are simplified such that they can
be displayed as the sum of a limited number (`max_panels`) of heat maps;
often without loss in accuracy.

![The four components of a fitted model: three curves and one heat map,
with the true functions drawn over the
curves.](reference/figures/README-lead-figure-1.png)

The figure shows a model fitted to simulated data,
``` math
y = 1 + \sin(\pi x_1) + 2(x_2^2 - 1/3) + x_3/2 + 2x_1x_2 + \text{noise},
```
with a fourth predictor `x4` that has no effect. The model found the
four true components and nothing else, in one call:

``` r

model <- rpf(y ~ ., data = sim)
```

## Why use it

- **Interpretability & Accuracy** A random planted forest can be fully
  visualized and provides state-of-the-art accuracy. By default the fit
  prunes irrelevant terms such that the fit is easier to comprehend and
  only keeps relevant terms.

- **No tuning needed** While some parameters can be changed, random
  planted forest works very well in its default settings and needs no
  tuning.

- **Instead of a GAM or GA²M.**

  - You do not specify the interactions: the forest finds which pairs
    and triples matter.
  - Smoothness is not assumed.

- **When it does not fit.**

  - Outcomes driven by interactions of many predictors (images, text)
  - Data too large (if memory or computational time is an issue one can
    reduce the number of families `n_families` and the maximal order of
    interaction `max_interaction`; usually at the cost of some accuracy)
  - Complex data (work in progress): e.g. time series, dependent rows,
    survival data etc.

### Benchmark: WIP

A comparison of accuracy and fitting time with random forests, boosting
and GAMs on public data sets will be added here.

## What the default does

A plain `rpf(y ~ ., data)` takes three steps, each with its own switch:

1.  **Grow** 200 tree families of up to three-way interactions, choosing
    the number of splits out of bag while they grow (`n_splits = NULL`).
2.  **Prune** the forest’s components to those that matter, with the
    rule and threshold chosen out of bag (`prune = TRUE`).
3.  **Simplify**: every kept three-way component is coarsened such that
    it can be visualized as the sum of at most 10 heat maps, and the
    model is pruned again (`max_panels = 10`).

## Installation

From [r-universe](https://plantedml.r-universe.dev/randomPlantedForest):

``` r

install.packages("randomPlantedForest", repos = "https://plantedml.r-universe.dev")
```

or from [GitHub](https://github.com/PlantedML/randomPlantedForest):

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("PlantedML/randomPlantedForest")
```

## Regression

Ozone in New York, from daily temperature, wind and sunlight:

``` r

library(randomPlantedForest)

air <- na.omit(airquality)
set.seed(1)
ozone <- rpf(Ozone ~ ., data = air)
ozone
#> ── Random Planted Forest model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Regression. Prediction = intercept + the sum of 4 components.
#> Intercept: 47.1412
#> 
#> Components (largest first), importance = share of the variance of the prediction on the training rows:
#>  component importance
#>  Temp      41%       
#>  Wind      32%       
#>  Temp:Wind 13%       
#>  Solar.R   3.1%      
#> 
#> How it was chosen:
#>   The forest: 200 tree families of 35 splits (chosen out of bag; growing stopped at 35).
#>   From the forest's 25 nonzero components (purified): those with a share of at least 1% of the forest's Var(prediction), each with one coefficient, fitted out of bag (rule R).
#>   Rule and threshold chosen by out-of-bag error (1-SE rule; 5 folds, seed 682372961) among 16 candidates.
#>   Left out: 21 components, shares together 2.9% (largest Month, 0.83%).
```

[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) returns a tibble,
and
[`predict_components()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/predict_components.md)
the components, which add up to it:

``` r

predict(ozone, head(air, 3))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred
#>   <dbl>
#> 1  31.0
#> 2  22.8
#> 3  17.4
head(predict_components(ozone, head(air, 3))$m)
#>      Solar.R        Wind      Temp Temp:Wind
#>        <num>       <num>     <num>     <num>
#> 1:  2.062333   1.8646920 -16.29678 -3.804457
#> 2: -3.976785   0.9708856 -15.70053 -5.606435
#> 3: -1.213864 -10.5361640 -15.41624 -2.609963
```

## Classification

``` r

penguins <- na.omit(palmerpenguins::penguins)
set.seed(1)
by_sex <- rpf(sex ~ ., data = penguins)
predict(by_sex, head(penguins, 3))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   .pred_female .pred_male
#>          <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1        0.161      0.839
#> 2        0.541      0.459
#> 3        0.774      0.226
```

## Learn more

- [Get
  started](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/randomPlantedForest.html):
  fit, print, predict, read the components.
- [Reading the
  model](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/reading-the-model.html),
  [How the forest is
  grown](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/growing.html).
- [The number of splits and further
  tuning](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/number-of-splits-and-tuning.html),
  [Pruning to a sparse
  model](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/pruning.html),
  [Classification](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/classification.html).
- [Speed, memory and saving
  models](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/speed-and-memory.html).
- The [glex](https://plantedml.com/glex/) package plots the components
  and computes other explanations from them.

## Citation

Hiabu, M., Mammen, E., & Meyer, J. T. (2020). Random Planted Forest: a
directly interpretable tree ensemble. arXiv preprint arXiv:2012.14563.
<https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2012.14563>

`citation("randomPlantedForest")` gives the BibTeX entry.

# Package index

## Fitting and prediction

Fit a model, predict with it, and print it.

- [`rpf()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf.md)
  : Random Planted Forest
- [`predict(`*`<rpf_pruned>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/predict.rpf_pruned.md)
  : Predictions of a pruned Random Planted Forest
- [`predict(`*`<rpf>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/predict.rpf.md)
  : Predict with a Random Planted Forest
- [`print(`*`<rpf_pruned>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/print.rpf_pruned.md)
  : Print a pruned Random Planted Forest
- [`print(`*`<rpf>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/print.rpf.md)
  : Print a Random Planted Forest

## Reading the model

The components that add up to the prediction, and the purification that
makes them unique.

- [`predict_components()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/predict_components.md)
  : The components of a Random Planted Forest's prediction
- [`purify()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/purify.md)
  [`is_purified()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/purify.md)
  : Purify a Random Planted Forest

## Pruning

Leave out the small components, by a rule chosen out of bag or by
cross-validation.

- [`prune_components()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/prune_components.md)
  : Prune the components of a Random Planted Forest

## The number of splits and tuning

The out-of-bag error along the splits, and the search over the
greediness and the leaf size.

- [`oob_path_checkpoints()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/oob_path_checkpoints.md)
  : Checkpoints of the out-of-bag path
- [`tune_control()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/tune_control.md)
  : Settings of the out-of-bag tuning
- [`greediness_ladder()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/greediness_ladder.md)
  : The greediness ladder of the out-of-bag tuning

## Looking inside a tree family

Draw the trees of one family, or get its leaves as boxes.

- [`plot(`*`<rpf>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/plot.rpf.md)
  : Plot a tree family
- [`rpf_boxes()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf_boxes.md)
  : Extract the boxes of a tree family

## Saving and restoring

Models hold a C++ object, which needs marshalling to survive
[`saveRDS()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/readRDS.html) or a worker process.

- [`rpf_marshal()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf_marshal.md)
  [`rpf_unmarshal()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf_marshal.md)
  : Serialize and restore Random Planted Forests
- [`rpf_is_valid()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf_is_valid.md)
  : Check whether a model's C++ forest is still alive
- [`bundle(`*`<rpf>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/bundle.rpf.md)
  [`bundle(`*`<rpf_pruned>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/bundle.rpf.md)
  : Bundle a Random Planted Forest

## Utilities

Compact printing of the flattened forest (`export_forest = TRUE`).

- [`print(`*`<rpf_forest>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/print.rpf_forest.md)
  [`str(`*`<rpf_forest>`*`)`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/print.rpf_forest.md)
  : Compact printing of forest structures

# Articles

### Get started

- [Getting Started with
  randomPlantedForest](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/randomPlantedForest.md):

  A first model, its predictions and components, classification, and the
  settings you may want.

### Understanding the model

What a fitted model is made of, and how the forest behind it is grown.

- [Reading the
  model](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/reading-the-model.md):

  The components of a fitted model, what the printed summary says line
  by line, importance, plots with glex, and how a component of three
  predictors is shown.

- [How the forest is
  grown](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/growing.md):

  Tree families, max_interaction, how a split grows a family, the split
  structures, candidates and aging, shown on one small family and
  checked on data where the truth is known.

### Fitting

The choices
[`rpf()`](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/reference/rpf.md)
makes for you, how it makes them, and how to change them.

- [The number of splits and further
  tuning](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/number-of-splits-and-tuning.md):

  How rpf() chooses the number of splits out of bag while the forest
  grows, when it stops, how to fix the number yourself, and what
  rpf(tune = ) searches.

- [Pruning to a sparse
  model](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/pruning.md):

  Why rpf() prunes the forest’s components, what it leaves out, the
  rules and the threshold, choosing them out of bag or by
  cross-validation, the display of three-way components, and prune =
  FALSE.

- [Classification](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/classification.md):

  Binary and multiclass outcomes, probabilities and classes, the
  components on the scale of the scores, and the losses.

### In practice

Large data, saving models, and other frameworks.

- [Speed, memory and saving
  models](https://plantedml.com/randomPlantedForest/articles/speed-and-memory.md):

  Threads, what the time and memory grow with, saving and restoring
  models, and using rpf() with tidymodels and mlr3.
